memory_update.text: WEST is the cleanest US-listed direct exposure found for the B2B coffee/tea/extract/private-label beverage solutions node, but follow-up must focus on profitability, leverage, Conway utilization, and commodity pass-through quality.

FARM and JVA are direct but micro-cap speculative exceptions; both require strict liquidity, balance-sheet, cash-flow, customer concentration, and exchange-listing checks before moving beyond Layer 1.

The node has two distinct public-market mappings: integrated beverage solutions/co-manufacturing platforms like WEST, and route-based foodservice coffee/tea distributors like FARM. These should be scored separately in later layers.

Private competitors and customers such as Ventura Foods, Golden State Foods, restaurant chains, Sysco, and US Foods may reveal demand and customer-dependency signals even when the direct supplier is not public.

WEST is the cleanest direct public-market candidate for the B2B coffee, tea, extracts, and private-label beverage solutions node, but must be screened for debt, capex ramp, customer mix, and commodity coffee pass-through.

JVA is a micro-cap speculative exception with direct wholesale/private-label coffee exposure; survival into later layers requires proof of foodservice/private-label mix, liquidity adequacy, and margin resilience.

Equipment vendors such as MIDD can be second-order beneficiaries of beverage menu expansion because coffee, espresso, cold beverage, and dispensing capacity require commercial equipment, installation, service, and replacement cycles.

Farmer Bros. would have been a high-relevance underfollowed candidate, but current public-listing status is uncertain due to possible 2026 take-private/delisting; verify with Nasdaq/SEC before treating it as investable.

Need a follow-up search for public co-manufacturers and private-label beverage manufacturers after TreeHouse Foods' apparent take-private process, because former public leaders may no longer be investable.
WEST is the cleanest US-listed pure play for integrated coffee, tea, extract, and private-label beverage solutions in restaurants and foodservice.
FARM is a small/micro-cap, low-attention direct foodservice coffee distributor and equipment servicer worth watching as an underfollowed node name.
The public universe for this node is thin; the best second-order exposure often hides in equipment, dispensing systems, and broad foodservice distributors rather than obvious consumer coffee brands.

WEST is the highest-priority direct public candidate for the B2B coffee, tea, extracts, and private-label beverage solutions node; next layer should scrutinize debt, capex, customer concentration, green-coffee hedging, and Beverage Solutions capacity utilization.
PFGC is not a manufacturer but may be an overlooked distribution-channel read-through for beverages and office coffee service inside broader food-away-from-home distribution.

Farmer Bros. appears no longer suitable for the active US-listed universe due to acquisition/delisting in May 2026, but its historical filings remain useful for mapping foodservice coffee economics, direct-store-delivery networks, coffee equipment service, and green-coffee input risks.

TreeHouse Foods had private-label beverage, coffee, and tea relevance, but current search context suggests it may have been taken private; verify current listing status before using THS as an active public candidate.
